name: Cerebral
one_liner: Online therapy and medication management for anxiety, depression and insomnia, by subscription or insurance; no controlled substances.
best_for: Adults with anxiety or depression who want non-controlled medication managed online
People who want therapy and medication in one monthly plan
People whose insurance is accepted (average copay about $30/session, per Cerebral)
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who need ADHD stimulants, benzodiazepines or other controlled medications (Cerebral no longer prescribes them)
People who don't want their data handled by a company under a 2024 FTC order over sharing health data with advertisers
short_description: Online therapy and non-controlled medication management by monthly plan or insurance; under a 2024 FTC order on health-data advertising.
long_description: Cerebral is a US telehealth company offering online therapy and medication management by video, phone and messaging, mainly for anxiety, depression and insomnia. It stopped prescribing controlled substances on 15 October 2022 and agreed not to prescribe them in future under a November 2024 non-prosecution agreement with federal prosecutors in Brooklyn, who said it had encouraged ADHD stimulant prescribing in 2021–2022; it forfeited about $3.65 million. In 2024 the FTC also reached an order with Cerebral after alleging it sent health information on nearly 3.2 million people to LinkedIn, Snapchat, TikTok and others through tracking tools and made cancelling hard; the order bans most use of health data for advertising and required about $7 million in refunds and penalties. Plans are monthly; Cerebral says insured patients pay an average $30 copay per session, and self-pay prices are shown on its plans page. No published study of Cerebral's own patients was found.
patient_summary: You sign up for a monthly plan, then meet a prescriber or therapist by video or phone and message your care team between visits. You can pay with insurance (Cerebral reports an average $30 copay per session) or self-pay, with therapy plus medication listed at about $365 a month; medications are paid for separately. It does not prescribe controlled substances.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance; self-pay therapy + medication about $365/month
pricing.notes: Cerebral says insured patients pay an average copay of $30 per session and extra therapy sessions are $135 each. Reviews put medication-only plans at about $60–$95/month; check cerebral.com/plans for the current rate. Medication costs are separate; FSA/HSA accepted.

basis.regulatory_action: FTC order, 2024: sent health information on nearly 3.2 million people to advertisers through tracking tools and made cancelling hard; about $7 million and a ban on most health-data advertising. DOJ non-prosecution agreement, 2024, over controlled-substance prescribing.

privacy.notes: Cerebral's policy still describes ad-platform vendors and personalised advertising with a 'Do Not Sell or Share' opt-out; care records fall under its HIPAA notice. A 2024 FTC order bans most use of health data for ads.

faqs.q: How much does Cerebral cost with insurance?
faqs.a: With insurance, Cerebral medication management typically costs $0-99/month depending on your plan. Without insurance, medication management is $99/month and therapy sessions are $199/month. Medication costs are separate and vary. The first month often includes an assessment fee of $49-99.

faqs.q: Does Cerebral prescribe controlled substances for ADHD?
faqs.a: Cerebral's ADHD prescribing policies have changed significantly since 2022. New patients seeking controlled substance ADHD medications face restrictions in many states. Cerebral now focuses primarily on anxiety, depression, and insomnia prescribing. Check current availability for your state before signing up.

Cerebral is a licensed telehealth provider with prescribers in most states. The company faced DEA and FTC investigations in 2022-2023 regarding prescribing practices, leading to policy changes. Current practices include more thorough evaluations and prescribing restrictions for controlled substances. Read recent reviews before signing up.

faqs.q: How does Cerebral compare to Done or Talkiatry?
faqs.a: Cerebral offers broader condition coverage (anxiety, depression, insomnia) while Done focused primarily on ADHD. Talkiatry provides more traditional psychiatry with longer appointments but higher costs. Cerebral's advantage is medication delivery and lower monthly costs with insurance.

primary_uses: Medication management for anxiety and depression (non-controlled)
Online therapy by video or phone
Messaging a care team between visits

availability.note: US only. No controlled-substance prescribing since October 2022 (made permanent by a 2024 non-prosecution agreement). Acquired Inflow in 2026 and centres ADHD care on therapy and coaching.
